hook.line: "I think he won't come" and "I'm not sure he'll come" feel close in English. In Spanish the verb shows how much you are committing.
hook.es: Tengo la impresión de que no vendrá.
hook.en: I have a feeling he won't come.

examples.es: Tengo la impresión de que no vendrá.
examples.en: I have a feeling he won't come.

examples.es: No estoy seguro de que venga.
examples.en: I'm not sure he'll come (a man speaking).

examples.es: Tengo la impresión de que Hernando tiene razón.
examples.en: I have a feeling Hernando is right.

examples.es: No estoy seguro de que Hernando tenga razón.
examples.en: I'm not sure Hernando is right (a man speaking).

examples.es: Tengo la impresión de que Altamira va a ganar.
examples.en: I have a feeling Altamira is going to win.

examples.es: No estoy segura de que Altamira gane.
examples.en: I'm not sure Altamira will win (a woman speaking).

rule:
A hunch leans one way. You are saying what you believe, so the verb is ordinary: *tiene*, *va a ganar*, *vendrá*.

A doubt does not lean. You refuse to commit, so the verb takes its "maybe" form: *tenga*, *gane*, *venga*.

*Tengo la impresión de que…* + ordinary verb
*No estoy seguro de que…* + "maybe" verb

Both keep *de que*; leave out the *de* and it sounds wrong. *Seguro* changes for a woman: *segura*.

In English both sound like "I think maybe". Spanish tells them apart by the verb.
smallPrint: Teachers say the indicative states a belief and the subjunctive leaves it open.

readAndPick.es: Tengo la impresión de que Hernando tiene razón.
options: I have a feeling Hernando is right.
I'm not sure Hernando is right.
Hernando is definitely wrong.

readAndPick.es: No estoy seguro de que Hernando tenga razón.
options: I'm not sure Hernando is right.
I have a feeling Hernando is right.
I'm sure Hernando is right.

readAndPick.es: Tengo la impresión de que Altamira va a ganar.
options: Altamira won, I'm sure.
I have a feeling Altamira is going to win.
I'm not sure Altamira will win.

readAndPick.es: No estoy segura de que Altamira gane.
options: I'm not sure Altamira will win (a woman speaking).
I have a feeling Altamira will win (a woman speaking).
I'm sure Altamira won (a woman speaking).

readAndPick.es: Tengo la impresión de que el concejo no escucha.
options: I have a feeling the council doesn't listen.
I'm not sure the council listens.
The council has no feelings.

readAndPick.es: No estoy seguro de que el concejo escuche.
options: The council listens, I'm sure.
I'm not sure the council listens (a man speaking).
I have a feeling the council doesn't listen.

readAndPick.es: Tengo la impresión de que la audiencia fue larga.
options: I have a feeling the hearing was long.
I'm not sure the hearing was long.
I didn't go to the hearing.

readAndPick.es: No estoy seguro de que la audiencia sea mañana.
options: I'm not sure the hearing is tomorrow (a man speaking).
I have a feeling the hearing is tomorrow.
The hearing is tomorrow, I'm sure.

yourTurn.prompt: Type the whole sentence, choosing *tiene* or *tenga*: Tengo la impresión de que Hernando ___ razón.
yourTurn.answer: Tengo la impresión de que Hernando tiene razón.
yourTurn.why: A hunch leans one way, so the verb is the ordinary *tiene*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type the whole sentence, choosing *tiene* or *tenga* (you are a man): No estoy seguro de que Hernando ___ razón.
yourTurn.answer: No estoy seguro de que Hernando tenga razón.
yourTurn.why: A doubt does not commit, so the verb takes its "maybe" form: *tenga*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it: "I have a feeling Altamira is going to win."
yourTurn.answer: Tengo la impresión de que Altamira va a ganar.
yourTurn.why: A hunch takes the ordinary verb after *de que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it as a woman: "I'm not sure Altamira will win."
yourTurn.answer: No estoy segura de que Altamira gane.
yourTurn.why: A doubt takes *gane*, and a woman says *segura*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it as a man: "I'm not sure the hearing is tomorrow."
yourTurn.answer: No estoy seguro de que la audiencia sea mañana.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the hunch into a doubt, as a man: Tengo la impresión de que no vendrá.
yourTurn.answer: No estoy seguro de que venga.
yourTurn.why: The doubt swaps the frame and puts the verb in its "maybe" form: *venga*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the doubt into a hunch that he is coming: No estoy seguro de que venga.
yourTurn.answer: Tengo la impresión de que viene.
accept: Tengo la impresión de que vendrá.
Tengo la impresión de que va a venir.
yourTurn.why: The hunch brings back the ordinary verb: *viene*.

pitfalls.wrong: No estoy seguro de que viene.
pitfalls.right: No estoy seguro de que venga.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A doubt does not commit, so the verb takes its "maybe" form: *venga*.

pitfalls.wrong: Tengo la impresión de que venga.
pitfalls.right: Tengo la impresión de que viene.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A hunch leans one way, so the verb stays ordinary: *viene*.

pitfalls.wrong: Tengo la impresión que no vendrá.
pitfalls.right: Tengo la impresión de que no vendrá.
pitfalls.why: Almost. This frame keeps its *de*: *impresión de que*.

personal: Say something you have a feeling about (a team, the weather, a friend's plans) with *Tengo la impresión de que…*. Then say something you are not sure about with *No estoy seguro de que…*.
